apartments.name: Stadium View Apartments
apartments.address: 400 Marion Pugh Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: James Griffiths
recentReviews.text: Our Aggie son has lived here the last two years.  We chose this based on location to TAMU and proximity to school bus stop(s). Easy plentiful parking by units. Quick and easy drive, bike or bus to school as needed. He has the larger one bedroom furnished unit. Attached an example photo of stainless kitchen appliances. The front office staff and properly management are very responsive and easy to work with.  Our son feels like a valued customer. Recommend this quiet complex for any Aggie.

recentReviews.author: Ana
recentReviews.text:
The rent is cheap, the roomates they pair me up with match well with my personality, the pool is gorgeous, and the events the apartment manager hosts are fun.
Ethan and Mkayla are always friendly when I pick up my mail, and our maintenance guys Chris and Bryce are pretty on the ball with responding to maintenance requests and fixing things up.

I'd say this is a good place to live if you want a good amount of space, don't mind living with a roomate, and have a tight budget. You can live pretty comfortably in College Station for $14/hr. I was surprised.

recentReviews.author: Awab Gabir (AwabTheMan)
recentReviews.text: The rent is cheap and the staff is fantastic!! If you're hit with financial difficulties, the staff will try their absolute best to accommodate you. You won't feel weird about it since you hang out at the office to chat and joke around, and you'll get to know the staff personally. Other properties might have better amenities, but Stadium View's real amenity is the staff itself.

apartments.name: REV Northgate Student Living
apartments.address: 315 College Main St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Kim K
recentReviews.text:
So far, the Rev has been an outstanding experience.  The staff made move in day so easy. The company they hired to help transport everything to the apartments was so helpful and efficient.  We really appreciated that the moving company left some of the large transport boxes on the first floor for residents to use after move in day for anything else that needed to be moved in by the residents throughout the weekend.

We had a very small issue that needed to be addressed in the apartment on move in day, and despite how busy everything was that day, maintenance was up to help out within an hour and fixed the issue! The apartment was super clean and totally move in ready.

Since move in, the staff has been so friendly, and there is always someone who actually answers the phone when you call the main number with a question, which is really nice.  The amenities here are awesome, but the staff really sets this place apart.

recentReviews.author: Patience Johnson
recentReviews.text: Genuinely the worst place I’ve EVER lived. They will seem so nice and so helping until you’re fully signed and moved in and then the staff and management are some of the rudest people I’ve ever interacted with. They also are constantly getting new staff and getting rid of the old one so no one knows how to do anything or any answers to any questions . They will basically bully and badger you to resign after only living there A MONTH. Maintenance can just come into your apartment with no warning what so ever. They once left a HUGE hole in my bathroom wall for about a week, and I had a cat there so I was very upset when they A) didn’t notify me and B) didn’t even close the bathroom door to ensure my cat couldn’t get in the hole. Maintenance also multiple times came into my apartment and then left trash. If you send an email to any manager, you will genuinely NEVER get a response. There was literal trash in the concrete of my ceiling (photos will be added). The front office people straight up lied to my face about a promo I was supposed to get when I signed my lease. I went my first month and a half without an oven because maintenance just couldn’t be bothered to contact the manufacture to fix something that took, and I’m not even kidding, five minutes to fix. Half the time the pool is down (don’t let whatever bs the owner will say fool you, it’s down A LOT). The only thing I will say they did good is they added cameras in the hallways (AFTER multiple complaints of things getting stolen off of doors or the hallways being utterly trashed at random). And it seems they finally managed to fix the elevators after about a year, because they used to be down every other day. That being said this was still my worst apartment experience. It’s so unbelievably overpriced for the cheap building that it is, and the management and staff are laughably incompetent.

recentReviews.author: J P
recentReviews.text:
After speaking with past residents, I was prepared for a very different experience. But from the moment we arrived, everything was A+ across the board. The entire team went above and beyond helpful, accommodating, and genuinely caring. The movers were outstanding: efficient, friendly, and even went the extra mile by taking trash down for us as a courtesy. I was blown away by the level of service. If I could give more than 5 stars, I absolutely would. This move-in deserves a 10 STAR rating! Other student living communities could learn a lot from how the REV treats its residents.

The only downside is the front door has not been locked yet. That poses security issues in my opinion. I would recommend having those locked at all times.

~ The Pizza Guy

apartments.name: U Club Townhomes on Marion Pugh
apartments.address: 801 Marion Pugh Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Lolol Oololl
recentReviews.text: The hot tub never works! Have put in multiple requests and it gets fixed for one day and then it stops. ITS NOT EVEN HOT! Pool and hot tub maintenance is horrible. They only clean it for the first week and when it’s time to sign the leases. There’s always leaves and did I forget to mention the HOT TUB IS NOT HOT AT ALL!

recentReviews.author: Andres Gumucio
recentReviews.text: Outstanding customer service... I opted in for the early move in and signed a new lease agreement that required me to pay the early move-in fee but I got some travel dates wrong and had to call them up to try and reverse it. The front desk person reached out to the manager quickly and gave me a response within the hour. Very thankful and optimistic about living here!

recentReviews.author: Ethan Testerman
recentReviews.text:
This has been the worst apartment experience I've had throughout my undergrad. The management here has been negligent towards fixing an issue they have caused and have been passive aggressive and unhelpful in resolving this issue.

Particularly, management staff lead under Danai Barnett. Danai herself has been very unprofessional, unhelpful, and extremely passive aggressive towards myself, other tenants in my unit, and my sponsors who attempted to aid them in fixing their issue towards setting up sponsored rental installments. Furthermore, the management staff provide round about answers that do not address questions asked or just leave questions and emails purposefully unanswered. If I had known it'd be like this, I'd have never considered the possibility of signing here.

I warn future residents, steer as far away as humanly possible unless you like a management team that wants your money and to make a mockery of you.

apartments.name: The Hudson at College Station
apartments.address: 410 Stasney St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Jack Ethridge
recentReviews.text: I have lived at the Hudson for 3 years. The building is convenient and fairly well-maintained, and the maintenance crew and staff are very helpful and kind. If you are considering living here, note that the students tend to trash the common areas (e.g., leaving food in plants, throwing drinks against doors, breaking exit signs, etc.). This is just what you have to expect living on Northgate in a massive apartment complex. Also, expect several incredibly loud fire alarm wake-up calls from people driving into pipes.

recentReviews.author: Davis Hipson
recentReviews.text:
I lived at The Hudson for 3 years, and I thoroughly enjoyed my whole time here. The units are very nice, the maintenance team is STELLAR (I never waited more than 24 hours for a request), and the entire office is approachable and nice. Many of the “cons” I’ve heard people associate with this apartment are largely just the price you pay for living on Northgate (rowdy neighbors, trash by the pool, etc.). The only bad things I can say about this complex is

A) the gates for the garage broke pretty frequently
B) the gym is okay, but could use a couple new machines

Besides that, I think the combination of luxury, proximity to Northgate/Campus, and affordability (compared to other NG properties) make this complex fantastic. I would HIGHLY HIGHLY recommend this place to any student. I’m going to miss it!

recentReviews.author: Steve Blazejewski
recentReviews.text:
Terrible experience.  Unit was clearly not inspected prior to move in.  Floors dirty, walls dirty, appliances banged up.  Dishwasher had standing water, was rusty, and smelled.  Luckily they replaced that day one.   They refuse to clean the carpet despite clear pet stains all over.

Management does nothing but deflect and try to avoid any action.

apartments.name: The Callaway House
apartments.address: 301 George Bush Dr W, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Lyric Taylor
recentReviews.text: I had an amazing dorm tour! The rooms were clean and spacious, and the common areas felt super welcoming. Personally loved the addition of the pool! The guide Austin was friendly and gave great insight into student life. I can really see myself living here definitely excited about the possibilities!

recentReviews.author: Ashley Jimenez
recentReviews.text: Steven is the best maintenance worker we have!!! Always is a friendly face to see in the hallways and fixes everything for us so fast! 222 owes him we love him!

recentReviews.author: Cole Chance
recentReviews.text: Do not live here unless you like overpaying. I lived here in the 2024-25 school year and it was not a pleasant stay. It smells like mold everywhere, the furniture hasn’t been updated in 10 years, the ac units barely work, I had $1100 in boots stolen from my room and staff was not helpful/did nothing about it, they do not care about you they only care about your money. Do not live here

apartments.name: 12 North Apartments
apartments.address: 301 Church Ave, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Collin Hernandez
recentReviews.text: You get exactly what you expect when you move here. The floor plans are small but are definitely manageable. Most importantly it is a very convent walk to any of your classes on campus while still being off campus and living the Northgate life. The staff is very caring and wants to always improve.

recentReviews.author: Breeanna Smith
recentReviews.text:
This is my second year at 12 North. It is very convenient to campus, and I am able to walk to all of my classes. 12 North also has a bunch of events going on for residents throughout the year, so those are always fun to attend. I live in a Premium B with my best friend from high school and it has worked out well considering these flats are pretty small compared to other apartments in the area.
However, it is a bit loud on the weekends when Northgate is poppin, which is not exciting because I am a light sleeper. I am in a Premium B and those are at the very end of the hallway facing directly out towards Northgate/campus. Nothing white noise and ear plugs can't fix though... or a headband with speakers in it - I've used these recently, playing white noise, and I don't hear Northgate at all.
Aside from noise, it is really nice to be able to walk to class and not have to drive in this overpopulated town.

recentReviews.author: Maggie Kaw
recentReviews.text: I love living at 12North! Amenities are great, the rent is great and most importantly it’s super close to classes as a science major. It’s also nice to be so close even when going out with friends.

apartments.name: U Centre at Northgate
apartments.address: 907 Cross St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Cole Cieslewicz
recentReviews.text:
Lived at U Centre for 3 years while attending A&M for Engineering, and it exceeded my expectations.  Staff are always super nice, very helpful, and a joy to deal with.  Maintenance (though rarely needed) is similarly responsive and non-intrusive.  Amenities are very well taken care of (gym, pool, grills).  Mail & packages are super easy to get/deal with.  AC/heat works well, floors are easy to clean, appliances are updated & are quickly replaced when broken.

Units themselves are well designed and feel very nice (crown molding is hard to come by in CStat!).  One complaint there is that the kitchens are set back from the windows and makes it dark, so make sure to get some under-cabinet lights online.  Rooms are spacious enough, have bare minimum furniture (but not much extra needed, but get more lighting).  Bathrooms are good.  Invest in rugs/carpets and lighting and this apartment will feel very homey.

TLDR: It's expensive, but especially for North/East campus-goers, I can't recommend it enough.

recentReviews.author: saishab das
recentReviews.text: I absolutely loved staying there. The location is perfect! All the staff members are super nice and helpful. This one time I paid my rent a little late so it ended up adding late fees, but upon requesting they removed it as a courtesy. The amenities are nice, and the maintenance was quick. However, I think the rent is going up very quickly. If they can keep the rent a little low, this place worth 6 Stars!

recentReviews.author: ssom
recentReviews.text: The apartment was nice and conveniently located near the campus. However, be aware that they charge for various things when you move out. To avoid unexpected fees, I recommend taking detailed photos of your room, common areas, and even the walls. Despite staying for only two months, I was charged for issues with the paint that I did not cause.

apartments.name: Callaway Villas
apartments.address: JM26+FM9, 305 Marion Pugh Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Dr. Karla Hernandez DeCuir
recentReviews.text: We recently visited Callaway Villas and did a tour with Sarah. Even though we have already signed a lease, she was super helpful, very friendly and provided outstanding service. She was very detailed and took us through all the spaces in the complex. She was phenomenal and we loved the place. My husband even said he wishes his dorms were that nice in college and will be visiting my son often (jokes) because it’s so nice and clean

recentReviews.author: Vivianne Cornell (Viv Cornell)
recentReviews.text: Calloway Villas is a wonderful place to live! Favorite part is being so close to campus. Great amenities like a gym and big pool and study spaces. Maintenance is usually really good about service requests. Friendly front desk staff and special shoutouts to Kyla, Bella, Rose, and Alex. They’ve all been super friendly and timely with everything I needed! Renewing my lease is easy!

recentReviews.author: Rosi Carvalho
recentReviews.text:
My daughter and I visited Callaway Villa twice before making the decision, precisely to make sure it would be a good place for her to live. During the tour (open house), we were warmly welcomed and were very pleased with what was presented to us.
However, after she received the key, I unfortunately identified three issues that left me dissatisfied:
The villa does not exactly match what was shown to us, especially the bathroom and kitchen.
The Washing machine makes an excessive noise, similar to a lawnmower, and the laundry room door does not close, making it impossible to reduce the noise. (My initial concern was the noise from the train, but this ended up being even more disturbing).
The gate to access the bus stop is very far. Students must walk a long distance under the strong sun, when there could be a gate closer to the bus stop to make the commute easier.

apartments.name: OTTO Northgate
apartments.address: 401 First St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Blake Helms
recentReviews.text: My move into The Otto has been such a great experience! The team was so accommodating — they even let me move in early, which made the process so much easier. They helped with the move and made sure everything went smoothly, even while keeping an elevator available for residents. On the official move-in day, my sister moved in as well and had the same seamless experience. The apartment itself was spotless and ready for us right away. I’m so glad I chose The Otto — highly recommend!

recentReviews.author: Amy Miller
recentReviews.text: What an amazing experience! The Otto is first class in everything they do! The move in process was flawless- the movers were the utmost professional and had our car unloaded and delivered to my son’s room in 5 minutes. We were able to enjoy the experience by helping him set up his new apartment and enjoy the experience without the stress of hauling items up stairs, elevators, etc! They literally thought of every detail- even provided lunch and an open bar for the parents on move  in day! What a blessing! I’m so thrilled my son chose to live here! Thank you Otto for making this a wonderful move in weekend for parents and students!!

recentReviews.author: Nikki Rijken
recentReviews.text: Daughter has been here for 2 years, spent her first year at Rev. OTTO has a bit quieter, more chill vibe. No problems at all with parking, secure and available. Maintenance responds same day and in her experience issue is fixed within 24 hours. Amenities galore, clean and very well maintained. Truly no complaints. It's expensive, but the value is solid.

apartments.name: The Landing College Station
apartments.address: 800 Marion Pugh Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Youmna S
recentReviews.text:
Stay away from this place. This has been the WORST apartment I have ever lived in BY FAR. I regret signing here with a passion. I got a 1 bedroom and 1 bathroom and pay around 1400 for the oldest and non functional apartment ever.

Upon move in the apartment was the dirtiest and trashiest place I’d ever seen. Spiderwebs and spiders were falling on my hand as I was trying to open the door. I had to stay in a hotel for 2 days and cancel the moving services so they could clean it. The day comes where I am supposed to move in after they cleaned it, and guess what? They STILL hadn’t cleaned it.

I have put in request for maintenance and talked to the manager/supervisor at the office to get things fixed in the apartment. I was supposed to be out of town but canceled plans so maintenance could come to work on my apartment today as promised, but guess what? They never came.

There are only TWO maintenance guys for this entire complex.

The model they show you before moving in looks nothing like the apartment.

I’ve had a constant buzzing sound in my apartment, turned out wires from the electricity cord were loose, I had to call emergency maintenance multiple times for them to come out and fix it because it was a safety hazard. When i told the supervisor about this she was like “we fixed it” instead of apologizing that I had to live with that for days. They literally have the worst attitude and will not admit accountability. Also they refuse to meet you and when they do, they keep you waiting around like a dog until they feel like seeing you.

- There is no fan or venting mechanism in the kitchen. I have NEVER in my life seen an apartment like that.
- I have a LITERAL light bulb in the fridge. Abnormal. Safety hazard. Blocks the entire first shelf.
- The washer and dryer are extremely dirty and make the weirdest cranking sounds. The washer literally ripped my bed sheets.
- There’s a code to unlock the door and multiple times it has not worked and I have been locked out
- The stove, only one of the rings works the rest are old and release smoke
- They don’t assign you to the floor you want to be on
- Sockets are coming off the wall.
- I cant order anything because we STILL don’t have mailboxes

There is literally not one positive thing about this place. With the amount I am paying you can live in a way newer complex with better services and amenities. The appliances here are the worst I have ever seen.

I could go on and on. I am writing this review as I have been patient with getting my problems fixed. Every time you promise to fix an issue on a specific day and not follow through is unacceptable.

Apparently these apartments have been built in the 80s. Sign here if you still want to live in that time period.

I want ALL my problems addressed and most importantly my door to be fixed.

recentReviews.author: Joshua T
recentReviews.text:
AWESOME!!!

I lived there 8 years and absolutely loved it! The staff is amazing. Perfect location for students at Texas A&M University.

Maintenance was fantastic! Josh Ford is the best.

Property Manager Kimberly O'Connell, Maddie, and the staff were always so wonderful. The team has a texting thread and they are prompt in responding.

You will totally be missed!

recentReviews.author: John Miller
recentReviews.text:
2 YEARS
• There was a shooting seven minutes away while I was living here.

• I have heard of people living with no AC

• Cannot get in touch with management when I have a roomate who lies and “borrows” my things.

• came back from school one day and saw police investigating the garbage Pulling out what looked like to be a gun.

• I have had ants, roaches living in the oven,

• Requested quiet and clean roommates, i got a messy late night, loud gaming, Whose girlfriend lives with us in our requested Male-only apartment.

• no help from management.

•  Not enough insulation in the ceiling the upstairs neighbors will bring people over and stay up late. They sound like elephants.

• If you thought this was a nice quiet place to live close to campus where you can study peacefully think again, consider that I have had to deal with a Chevy Silverado who opens all their doors and windows and blast music while drinking beers past midnight revving the trucks engine.

• paid for a lease with delay in access to amenities.

• They constantly switch the rules on visitor parking (So if you’re a parent, be careful, this place will turn a wholesome memory to a nightmare, I am a resident and I got towed, (they resolved that) And My Fiancée, who would come regularly also got towed).

• But after tons of complaints, They decided to remove some visitor parking. The problem was that people would park there to go to the football games so what they did is started game day parking. This was news to me after I signed my lease I had no idea the parking lots we had access to would be turned into what seems to be a SIDE BUSINESS!?!

• If you get the older housing (instead of the Luxe) You will need blackout curtains taped to your wall To truly block the light. Without it, it looks like it’s daytime 24/7 They place obnoxiously bright sketchy white LED lights Right in front of the window of the entrance.

• We had a clogged sink that started smelling and flooding that we didn’t get any help for for a week.

• The crazy part about the parking is there are a lot of open spaces Just not for visitors.

• I will gladly update this if I truly believe their service has improved. But I believe it is very important potential tenants understand what they’re signing up for and right now it’s not worth it’s price.

•understaffed in management, understaffed in maintenance.

• current parking. you need to sign up on an app and get visitor tag. It’s first come First serve on game days. Whether you’re going to the game or not. 9:00am bright and early. Its first come first serve I would get there at 5:00 am if you want to be first in line.  You likely won’t be able to get a visitor tag but you can pay a ridiculous amount of money.

They really did not like people using our parking lots to get to the Game, so they added the parking tags, an app to sign in to, and FOR SOME REASON GIVE OUTSIDERS AN OPTION TO PARK HERE FOR MONEY.

Make it make sense. Attached is a photo of the line

apartments.name: Ion College Station
apartments.address: 711 University Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Alina Torres
recentReviews.text:
I do not recommend.

I lived at Aspire last year and it was a pretty great experience. However, since it has become ION, there have been many issues. I understand that transition periods are tough but they have had no issues rebranding everything. Replacing all our apartment number signs, study room vinyl, and painting their logo on the walls.

However 2/3 of our elevators have been broken for weeks and there has been no rush to fix them. We usually have to wait 5 minutes for an elevator, and many have defaulted to taking the stairs (there are 15 floors by the way).

recentReviews.author: Ayden Dennis
recentReviews.text: Would not recommend living here at all. I lived here for two years and the new management is terrible. Many issues across the property (pool, gym equipment, outdoor TV, elevators, etc.) were always broken and took months to fix if they were fixed at all. Simple request such as receiving Amazon packages became a hassle as it would take hours for them to process them once delivered. Quality of washer/dryer and dishwasher is very poor and did a number on my clothes. Construction and build quality overall is poor and there have been a myriad of issues demonstrating this (my room flooded during finals week due to a leak in my ceiling, foundation issues regarding the pool).

recentReviews.author: I Love my GF
recentReviews.text:
DO NOT RENT HERE AT ALL COSTS!!!!

If I could give them negative 1.4 million stars, that wouldn't nearly be enough to qualify just how atrocious this apartment complex is.

1. The furniture sucks, it is torn up and shitty. It is literally just a crappy "sofa" (if you can even call it that) and a chair. Oops, almost forgot the uncomfortable stools they give you in the kitchen and the worst mattresses to exist (maybe ever). I have literally had to get surgery on my back since moving here because of the mattress.

2. The management is terrible. They are repeatedly disrespectful to their residents and blatantly go out of their way to avoid speaking to them. They are very insensitive, lack common courtesy, are very lackadaisical when it comes to fixing any issues their residents have. They also have the emotional intelligence of four year olds.

3. The price is RIDICULOUS. You pay at bare minimum far more than any other apartment complex in the area (this is true, get quotes), and on top of all that, are expected to pay an absurd (new phone's worth of money) "Community Fee" for the "amenities" that are almost never open due to maintenance issues.

4. The elevators are ALWAYS. I repeat ALWAYS broken. There has never been a time in which all elevators are working. At least 1, typically 2, are shut down.

5. The gym sucks. Some treadmills are broken (and have been for months), the equipment is battered, and there are pipes connected through the ceiling in the gym so you can hear whenever someone above you just flushed.

There's definitely more, but I don't have the time to expand because I have to hang out with my girlfriend. If you're going to get an apartment on Northgate that's right near north campus, go with the Rise. The workers clearly actually care about the product they uphold, and the amenities are way nicer for a lot lower of a price.

If Ion doesn't reply, assume the staff has swatted down my door and taken me hostage and are holding me in a cellar with all of their trash that they never take out.

apartments.name: Park Place Apartments
apartments.address: 1505 Park Pl, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Mansour Alnajrani
recentReviews.text:
I have lived in this apartment complex since September 2021 until the day I wrote this review. I have been in the USA for several years. I have lived in many apartments, and by far, this is the best one-bedroom apartment I have had.

First, the layout of the apartment is great. You have the living room and kitchen on the first floor, while the bedroom, walk-in closet, and bathroom are on the top floor. This setup is ideal because it allows you to organize your living space separately from your sleeping area, helping you stay productive without the temptation of your bed calling you to sleep.

The neighbors are nice, and everyone is friendly and minding their own business. Overall, the complex is calm, quiet, and free of excessive noise. Additionally, it is within walking distance of HEB, Target, Chase Bank, and several restaurants (~ 10-15 minutes away). If you are a student without a car, this location is especially convenient, as it saves you from frequently ordering food delivery and paying expensive fees (~ $15 per order). Also, it is close (~2 min) to bus 27, which takes you to the university

Lina, the property manager, is friendly and ensures that all residents' needs are met in a timely manner. She does an excellent job of selecting tenants to maintain a safe and welcoming community. During my nearly 3.5 years here, I have had only three minor maintenance issues, all of which were resolved either the same day or by the next day at the latest. Darvin, the maintenance technician, is hardworking and responds quickly to service requests, ensuring that issues are addressed promptly.

I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a comfortable and well-managed apartment.

recentReviews.author: Debra McKeown
recentReviews.text: Park Place is a quaint cluster of homes in a perfect location. The apartments are cozy with a convenient layout. The manager is responsive, professional, and kind. Maintenance, the few times needed, was carried out quickly and efficiently by a skilled craftsman. The atmosphere is quiet with a nice green space the leashed dogs enjoy. Parking is plenty and easy.  It's a great place to call home!

recentReviews.author: Prince Habeeboo
recentReviews.text: My stay at Park Place Apts was very pleasant. The apartment was clean, relatively remodeled and neat. I really liked the two level floorplan. The tenants were mostly students or bit elderly, very nice neighbors.  Maintenance guys were very nice and reasonably available when scheduled. Lina Alford, the complex manger was very easy to work with and well communicative! I highly recommend of this place. It was the only complex i have renewed my lease with there.

apartments.name: The Junction at College Station
apartments.address: 2415 Junction Boys Rd, College Station, TX 77845, USA

recentReviews.author: Hannah
recentReviews.text:
My roommates and I moved into The Junction in August 2023, and from the very beginning, we encountered multiple issues. Upon move-in, our unit was missing furniture, had clearly not been properly maintained, and had not been cleaned. One of the first and most serious problems was the air conditioning. Between August and September, our unit consistently stayed around 85 degrees. It took weeks before they finally placed window units in our bedrooms to temporarily resolve the issue.

In addition, the walls and doors had visible scratches and damage — from the previous tenants’ dog — and our balcony had clothes, old blankets, and sheets that had not been removed before we moved in.

We also experienced an ant infestation that took weeks of complaints before it was addressed. Our washer and dryer were broken, so we were forced to do laundry either at the clubhouse or at friends' houses. On top of that, we went several weeks without hot water — which is not only unacceptable but also a violation of basic housing standards. Management initially dismissed our concerns, claiming the water temperature was “fine.” It wasn’t until I threatened legal action that they finally investigated the issue. They later claimed they had no knowledge of the problem because they were away at a conference.

While we were eventually compensated for these issues, the amount we received didn’t come close to covering the inconvenience, discomfort, and lack of amenities we were promised in our lease.

Additionally, I had a package stolen while it was in the care of the staff. Although I was compensated for the loss, I had confirmation that a staff member had picked it up, and by the time I went to retrieve it, it had mysteriously disappeared.

We also had ongoing issues with other residents or guests dumping their trash into our bins located behind our unit. One of the rules at the Junction is that your trash must be in a trash bag or else it won't be collected, and that is how we knew it wasn't ours. When it came time to move out, The Junction told us it was our responsibility to clean up the area or we would be charged $30 per bag of trash they collected — even if it wasn’t ours.

That said, I do want to acknowledge that the management must have changed or brought in new staff, because many of the issues we faced were specific to the 2023–2024 lease term. My second year living at The Junction was great, and aside from the continued trash problem, I encountered no major issues.

Update: After receiving my move out statement I'm lowering my review. I was charged for over $200 worth of "damages" but my roommates and I left the apartment in better condition than when we moved in originally in 2023 (with proof). We repainted all of the damage that was previously there from past tenants (something the Junction should have done) and also heavily cleaned the whole apartment.

recentReviews.author: Ty Gore
recentReviews.text: Place looked great when toured it. On move in day however my apartment was still nasty and dirty. Maintence here is terrible and never gets anything done in a timely manner. When I moved out they proceeded to send me a 700 dollar cleaning and damage fee for the smallest stuff. Had a small paint scratch smaller than a penny and they charge 125 for it. They charged me 265 to replace mattress when there is nothing wrong with it. Don’t recommend unless who want to be attacked with BS fees. Then charge me 100 dollars to clean my bathroom after I deep cleaned it and charged me a carpet cleaning fee after I had steamed it.

recentReviews.author: Annika Langer
recentReviews.text: They will charge you for normal wear and tear upon moving out. Before moving out my roomate and I vacuumed every floor and carpet, I cleaned all my furniture and wiped down and cleaned my bathroom and was met with over $300 in damage charges for damages that were not even there to begin with. They are going scam you over non existent damage charges!

apartments.name: Rise at Northgate
apartments.address: 717 University Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Reeve Baker
recentReviews.text: The Rise has been a great experience. Although the rooms are small, the amenities are nice and visitor passes are handy. The management staff and team have been wonderful and very helpful.

recentReviews.author: Emily Nelson
recentReviews.text: It has a super convenient location and good facilities. Whenever something breaks, they always repair or replace it pretty quickly. The staff is always super friendly and helpful!

recentReviews.author: Michael Crow
recentReviews.text: I love living here, it’s quiet and I love having my own sense of personal space. With it being right across the street from the campus, it’s very convenient as well!

apartments.name: Campus Village Apartments
apartments.address: 1711 Harvey Mitchell Pkwy S Building, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Jordan McKenzie
recentReviews.text: I have lived here for two years and have re-leased for a third year. Since I have been here my rent has raised nearly $100. They also make you release within three months of your current lease. Utilities are very expensive and are on a shared meter with other apartments so you can't do much to lower your utility bill. Additionally, they started charging for water. They force you to register your car through a towing company whose site is unsecure and provide the towing company insurance info, VIN numbers, and forces your visitors to also register with them. They drive their noisy tow truck around the complex all night long. Over the summer, someone got shot in the head at the community pool, then a 20 minute police chase happened around the complex at 1:00 am. There is often police incidences her specifically around the pool area. Biggest issue is the noise at night. Staff is nice but often uninformed.

recentReviews.author: Cassidy Krieg
recentReviews.text: Love CV!!! I have had the best experience ever! The maintenance and front office is fantastic. They always get to anything as soon as possible. Me and my roommate have had the best housing here. Highly recommend to live at campus village!!!

recentReviews.author: Mia Putnam
recentReviews.text: I have lived at Campus Village for three years during my undergrad at Texas A&M and I highly recommend it to any students. I have had such a wonderful experience living here and I am especially appreciative of the kind and helpful staff. As well, the maintenance here is wonderful and replies very quickly (usually same day) to any issues. To any students looking for safe and good housing, I recommend CV!

apartments.name: Park West Apartments
apartments.address: 503 George Bush Dr W, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Alejandro P
recentReviews.text:
I would never recommend living at Park West. From the moment I moved in, the apartment was in terrible condition and it was clear that little to no effort had been made to prepare it for new residents. The floors were dirty, the fridge and stove were both filthy and outdated, and there was visible mold in the unit. The air conditioning was broken and completely unreliable, which made the place almost unlivable during the heat. On top of that, there were spider webs in the corners of the ceilings, showing that the place had not been cleaned properly at all.

The furniture they provide is equally unacceptable. The bed feels worse than a jail bed and that is not an exaggeration. It is uncomfortable, old, and clearly cheap. For the amount of money Park West charges, you would expect at least a basic level of comfort and cleanliness, but what I experienced was far below even the minimum standard.

Overall, this has been one of the worst housing experiences I have ever had. Management clearly does not care about the quality of their units or the wellbeing of their residents, and they continue to charge outrageous prices for conditions that are unsafe and unsanitary. Save yourself the frustration and stress and look for housing somewhere else. Park West is not worth it in any way

recentReviews.author: Astha Chitlangia
recentReviews.text:
I would not recommend living here. One of the biggest issues is that the AC is almost never on in the buildings. We’re in Texas heat, and it’s beyond unreasonable that tenants are expected to walk through lobbies and hallways that feel like ovens, especially when rent is already so high. It’s not just uncomfortable—it’s neglectful.

What makes it worse is that management doesn’t seem to care. Something as basic as keeping the common areas livable should be a priority, but instead, they cut corners and act like tenants are asking for too much. For the amount of money being paid, working AC in shared spaces should be the bare minimum, not some luxury.

On top of that, management is extremely hard to deal with. They’re unhelpful, dismissive, and make the simplest issues a headache to resolve. The lack of accountability and concern for residents is honestly embarrassing.

Overall, this place charges like a premium complex but delivers the bare minimum. Between the stifling heat in the buildings and the terrible management, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere before signing a lease here.

recentReviews.author: Christina Le-Tran
recentReviews.text: As a teacher/mother who pays almost 2000 a month for rent for my children, I have been quite disappointed this year. The biggest complaint is the lack of visitor parking available. My drive to TAMU is 2 hours. Both my children were sick, and I drove around waiting for a visitor parking to open and couldn't find parking for almost an hour. That is unacceptable. UNACCEPTABLE.  There were plenty of available parking around park west, but not for visitors. As a parent, please designate more visitor parking at your apartment. I will expect some resolution to this problem. Thank you.

apartments.name: White Creek Apartments
apartments.address: 225 Discovery Dr, College Station, TX 77843, USA

recentReviews.author: H. K. Lee
recentReviews.text:
My daughter has been living in White Creek for 2 years and she's planning to stay until her graduation; 1 more year. It's safe and convenient in all ways for a college life.
The apartment unit itself is very spacious and has lots of storage in the kitchen. 100% recommended!!

recentReviews.author: lizzie love
recentReviews.text:
It’s by far the nicest place to live on campus. I’ve absolutely loved living here and the area is so nice.
Pros:
- The Community center with a sand volleyball court behind it
- The Activity center where you can play ping pong or just study
- Pay by semester apartments that are quite nice.
- Own room, kitchen and a washer/dryer per apartment.
- Bus route to take you to main campus or it’s just a 15-20 minute walk to the MSC.

Cons:
- Mail. Sometimes getting your mail can be a headache.
- Parking. Getting a spot in 122a comes with a bit of luck. But 122b isn’t too far.
- Expensive. Definitely cheaper places to live off campus with more amenities. Even still the apartments are very nice.
- Late buses. The buses are late quite often.

recentReviews.author: Haley Lancaster
recentReviews.text: Way too expensive for what you’re getting! tiny rooms & NO PARKING was so annoying. Had to take the bus to main campus even though these apartments are still on campus. I didn’t like having an RA in an apartment still. Trash was really far from us, we had a long walk to get our trash bags to the trash room. Our dishwasher, oven/stove, and washer all broke in one year and each took over 2 weeks to fix & we only got $50 back from rent total when the washer broke & we were told that we would just need to find somewhere to do our laundry for now since they couldn’t fix it yet. I didn’t always feel super safe here either and the walls were super thin so it was loud all the time when people down the hall or outside were loud. It was decent, but i couldn’t wait to get out of there by the end of the year.

apartments.name: Aggie Station
apartments.address: 4151 Wellborn Rd, Bryan, TX 77801, USA

recentReviews.author: Chris Wolff
recentReviews.text:
Buyer beware! My son and his roommates were each charged a $300 “cleaning fee” at move-out — that’s $900 total for one apartment. The kicker? The apartment was clean when they left. In fact, it was dirtier when they moved in, and we even reported it to management at the time. Despite this, management brushed off our concerns and seemed far more interested in collecting fees than addressing the issue fairly.

This feels like a scam designed to squeeze money from students and their families. The experience was frustrating, unfair, and left us with the impression that Aggie Station does not operate in good faith. If you’re considering moving here, think twice. There are plenty of other complexes in College Station that treat residents with respect and honesty.

recentReviews.author: Vraj Patel
recentReviews.text:
Make sure to be careful of move-out charges. Charging my roommate and I for dust and for flakes that comes from their overly done popcorn textured ceiling, when we turned in the keys to the office well before inspection. Also charged for other cleanings where things were already clean. Even after explaining these things they refuse to take off the charges.

Update: You don't email aggie station, you have to email american campus. All they tell you is that your apartment did not meet requirements, but do not explain what exactly you were charged for even after asking multiple times. They also contradict their statements and do not answer any questions that you ask.

recentReviews.author: Marlenie Blanco
recentReviews.text: My car broke down when I went up there for a weekend and the service men, Cliff Lewis and Angel, were so helpful ! They were understanding of my situation and were super guiding. They showed up with a full set of tools and helped me out with no complaints just pure smiles ! Super awesome guys

apartments.name: The Gardens Apartments
apartments.address: 250 Calvin Moore Ave, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Yanxiu Ge
recentReviews.text:
Update: Paul, the current manager here forged my initials on an official document less than two years ago. The university stated no harm was caused so no record correction, though they admitted Paul forged my initials. I reported externally to multiple channels today.

I see from previous reviews that I’m not the only one complaining about the residence manager Paul. I’ve been living here for 9 years and had a few interactions with him, and none of them were positive. The first few times I thought it was just he was in a bad mood, but it’s impossible that he’s in a bad mood all the time, so it is just his unprofessionalism.
This guy keeps contradicting his own words and even once put my initials on official documents without my consent. If he ever does anything that is not strictly mentioned in the contract but slightly nice, even though it would require minimal effort from him, he would act like he did you a huge favor.
The apartment management should know that he would be one of the first few people some new students would interact at A&M, and at least a generally friendly manner would be expected.
The apartment itself is good. Close to campus and has a lot to offer.
Maintenance used to be quick and reliable, but it took them a month to fix my wall and change the dishwasher that was not functioning well, so it’s getting worse. I would give a 5 star rate 3 years ago, but not anymore.

recentReviews.author: Eugene Ku
recentReviews.text:
Gardens apartmenr single handedly makes me regret coming to TAMU already.

At night, a nearby miniature golf-course (popstroke) plays very loud music until 12 am everyday, making you feel like you are sleeping inside a club bathroom. Because of this I have gotten more nightmares in the past week than my entire life.

Basketball court is unusable with nets missing, water fountain broken, and big mud puddle awaiting to ruin your ball and your day.

Apartment is very dirty as they do not get cleaned when residents leave.

For the price you are paying at the gardens, you can get much cleaner apartment that is actually decent, has a swimming pool, and within close proximity.

recentReviews.author: Athul Manoharan
recentReviews.text:
The apartments are very near to the Zachary and ETB buildings. Very close to McDonald's and taco bell.

Convenient for engineering students, but far from the west campus. The rooms are very good. Apartment service is also good. Has an open access lab for students, volleyball court, basketball court etc. Fully furnished. One bed per bedroom, sofa set, table and chairs, refrigerator, oven , dishwasher etc are included. Common laundry.

apartments.name: Cambridge Hall
apartments.address: 501 University Oaks Blvd, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Justin Butler
recentReviews.text: Tour was great, Liliana is so patient and kind. Lease process was easy, they seem to be always ready to assist. So far so good move in 8/14

recentReviews.author: Kelsie McQuietor
recentReviews.text:
We moved my son in over the weekend. The elevator was out of order, and we saw a giant cockroach on the wall in the hallway. Hopefully, both things were just a fluke.

We also adjusted our schedule to move him in from 11-2 on Friday because they would not adjust the time. We came back the following day to move in more of his belongings in, and very few people were moving in. Thus, they definitely could have been more flexible with the move-in process.

recentReviews.author: Steve P
recentReviews.text: When I needed to find housing for my incoming freshman, I learned that Cambridge Hall was an option from another patent during NSC. I'm so glad I decided to visit! The staff is very friendly, the rooms are clean and well laid out, and it definitely had a college dorm feel, even though it is a half mile or so off of campus. The on-site gym, cafeteria,  movie room and pool are just icing on the cake!

apartments.name: The Standard at College Station
apartments.address: 315 Boyett St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: K MAC
recentReviews.text: All of these negative reviews are 100% accurate. The location and tour look great when you visit for the first time but the actual apartment you get is a joke. We are on our second year and it was a huge mistake. We will not be renewing. The new apartment was filthy when we moved in. We were told it was not their responsibility bc there was a renewal in the unit. That makes zero sense when we signed a new lease.  Multiple issues in the apartment that still haven’t been fixed. Holes and gashes in walls in the unit and in the hallways. Staff is unresponsive and rude when you do get in touch w them. Highly recommend you live anywhere but here.

recentReviews.author: Holly Gard
recentReviews.text: ZERO STARS!! This place is AWFUL!!!! My daughter’s apartment flooded their first night and no one would come to fix it. Then they dried out the nasty carpet and laid it back down. She had constant mold problems. Her bathroom plumbing never worked and was never fixed correctly. Now they are charging us for damages from the flood. DO NOT rent here! Literally a tent outside would be a better option!

recentReviews.author: Lj Davis
recentReviews.text: I have lived here for over a year. This place gets more hate than it deserves, its not amazing but it has a great location to campus and northgate, decent amenities, and the apartment units aren't too bad (compared to nearby alternatives). The main issues that you would face living here: Getting your packages takes a while as the front desk has to organize them first and then notify you, The gym equipment often breaks because of the braindead freshman who decide to use the apartment gym as a playground, the pool is on the roof which is cool but usually is gross. Overall not bad for a college campus apartment. I would recommend living in a top floor, everything bad such as flooding and mold seems to happen to people who live near the first floor.

apartments.name: The Stack at Legacy Point
apartments.address: 711 Church Ave #101, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: LD Hoover
recentReviews.text: The Stack has great management and staff! Harlan is a great manager always very responsive. Rudy, head of maintenance, is the best always taking care of any issues quickly. It is a great location right across from campus. Highly recommend!

recentReviews.author: Jennifer H.
recentReviews.text: Can not say enough positive things about The Stack! Students can walk to engineering building and there are restaurants,  CVS close by. Very quiet inside ( can hear church bells and Nortgate on weekends if on that side) and lots of study spaces. Maintenance has been wonderful, even on weekends. Mgmt has been great the past three years with lots of activities for students.

recentReviews.author: Justin Simms
recentReviews.text: The apartment is amazing! Love the staff and maintenance teams they are super fast and helpful.

apartments.name: Berkeley House at College Station
apartments.address: 801 Wellborn Rd, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Mendy Schneider
recentReviews.text:
Please let me start by sharing that I don't ever like leaving a negative review as I know we all have a bad day that we need grace extended for.  BUT with the lies and false accusations made towards a roommate's review, I feel I am left with no choice but to protect THEIR character, corroborate her story, and place the blame where it truly lies.  MOLD is an absolute issue at this property.  When, in the other review, the staff - specifically April Searcey - wants to claim they were not aware of the issue during the lease, she is sadly boldface lying in written form.  As she wants to lie in public on the web, we can respond with written proof where they were made aware of the issue during the lease term (ended July 21...you'll see pic July 21 where e-mail is asking me if I would like to follow up as my three e-mails had not been responded to).  Couch pic and decor pic July 1.
With everything we would report within our time there, they always want to point the finger back at you versus accepting responsibility.  As the parent, I was there when the maintenance guy came in and was dumbfounded by the mold growing everywhere and clueless how to resolve it that he was even taking pictures and sending them to his supervisor.  It was when my husband, who has owned a commercial construction company, arrived and could immediately point out where the issue was and that it was a leak in the ceiling.  They just repaired the Sheetrock but did NOT repair the leak.  So within a couple of days, the Sheetrock was wet again (pic attached).  I sent daily pictures and e-mails after the "repair," during the lease term, with NO RESPONSE from management.  They took out the moldy couch and just placed another couch in there KNOWING the leak was still active.  With zero response from them and me really just caring for the next set of teenagers to live there being exposed to this, I called the City for some type of accountability.  Our girls had a horrid cough and the third roommate was like, "I did notice I was having to use my inhaler a whole lot more."  So, with all the mold that was seen, there is so much more behind the walls unseen.  They know at some point in the year there was an issue with water and they had fans in hallways and such to dry it all out and one tenant kept turning off the fan/blowers because she didn't like the noise they made.  We know that because they made that troublemaker move in with our girls temporarily to try to get her to stop turning off the fans on her upper floor.  Supposedly a mold truck was there in their parking lot the other day.  Prayerfully they are getting to the root of the issue before others move in.  I would just strongly suggest you walk into this property, or any property managed by April Searcey, with your eyes WIDE OPEN.  She's a great sales lady and a master with words - it's the lack of authenticity to them that is brought into question by her actions or truly lack thereof.  There are many other things that I wasn't a fan of, but it doesn't put your health in extreme jeopardy like the above does.  No place is going to be perfect, but you can certainly choose to stay away from dangerous ones.
And cleanliness was not an issue on our girls' part.  One is OCD, the other just stays on top of it, AND I had a professional cleaner come in throughout their time there to do deep cleaning for them as well.

recentReviews.author: Alex Beane
recentReviews.text: Avoid all Student Quarters properties in College Station (The Hudson, Berkeley House, and Cherry Street). They use predatory leasing tactics that leave loyal tenants paying premiums while new tenants can sign leases for the exact same units for hundreds of dollars less. If you plan on finding a place to live for years, your rent *will* increase with no justification as amenities lay neglected and outdated, even if you're told otherwise when you sign your lease.

recentReviews.author: Hannah
recentReviews.text:
I hated living here at Berkeley House, and for a number of reasons:

Rent is absurd for what you paying for. I pay almost $1000 a month for a 4x4 because you have to pay for parking, and parking is terrible! You will likely never get a good spot and I pay $30 a month. The elevator is almost always broken and was broken for months! The wifi frequently goes down and it’s annoying when you have to study. There is barely any visitor parking, there is no easy way to get to TAMU without driving to a bus stop or paying for a parking pass so that’s extra $$$. Location is terrible with the train being next to the property and it gets so loud everyday I can hardly sleep. You can also hear every car passing by as the walls are so thin. There is something constantly being broken in the unit, whether it be the fridge, disposal, or laundry and we have to call maintenance very often. Honorable mention: they matched me with the most rude, disrespectful, and dirty roommates.

If I could move out early, I 100% would. I hate living here and will definitely be telling my friends to stay away.

apartments.name: The Zone
apartments.address: 2001 Holleman Dr W, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Mu-Jung Lee
recentReviews.text: Considering its distance to the campus, the rent is not too high. It’s just the rent gets higher and higher every year and it’s frustrating. The rent does not include utilities. The pool is pretty much public an it’s loud near the pool at noghts. I see nonresidents there every now and then.

recentReviews.author: Hakan ÇELİK
recentReviews.text: We would like to sincerely thank Ethan for everything he has done for us. From the very beginning, he went above and beyond to help us find the most suitable apartment. He took the time to understand our needs and made sure we got the best possible deal. Ethan put in extra effort to ensure we could benefit from a fair and affordable price, and that meant a lot to us. His positive energy and friendly attitude made the whole process smooth and enjoyable. Every time we spoke with him, his enthusiasm and professionalism truly stood out. It’s rare to meet someone who cares this much about making others comfortable. We always felt supported and valued thanks to his hard work and kindness. We are truly grateful for his dedication and patience throughout everything. Working with Ethan has been an absolute pleasure. Thank you for everything, Ethan. we’re so glad to have met you!

recentReviews.author: Kimaya Shikarkhane
recentReviews.text: Nice apartment complex with Aggie Spirit bus stop near by. We did have roach problem in the beginning but it was sorted after one pest control. Maintenance requests were always resolved in a timely manner. Apartment was also nice with properly functioning appliances.

apartments.name: The Enclave
apartments.address: 1800 Holleman Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Destiny Soto
recentReviews.text:
I was extremely disappointed to learn that The Enclave charged me a $150 late key return fee, despite being told in person—by staff and in front of witnesses—that I would not be charged as long as my belongings were removed before the unit walk-through.

Throughout my residency, I have been a respectful tenant and have never had any issues. The least I would expect is for management to honor their word. This is especially concerning given that no action was taken when I previously raised serious safety concerns after being harassed and threatened by another resident due to my status as a disabled veteran.

I respectfully request that this charge be removed from my account in accordance with the agreement made at move-out.

recentReviews.author: Bryan Byrd
recentReviews.text: DO NOT get a place here. This apartment is unsafe, poorly maintained, and the personnel do NOT CARE about the residents. My son and nephew stayed here. During their stay someone tried to break into their apartment, one of their bikes got stolen, the apartment complex towed one of their cars which had the permit and was parked in their designated spot. They refused to reimburse me the $300 to get the car back. Then to add insult to injury they charged my son and separately charged my nephew for the same "damages" or "clean up" after they moved out. When they moved in the apartment was a dump and the AC could never keep up. We put in a better microwave and had a cleaning service clean the apartment weekly. When we left, we left it spotless. We "donated" the microwave to the unit in addition to one that was there. Even with this they charged us $200 of BS stuff including mostly double charges with his roommate. If I could give ZERO STARS I would. Do not walk - run away!

recentReviews.author: Peter
recentReviews.text:
A Truly Living Experience! First, let's talk about the wildlife! Who needs expensive pest control when you get complimentary cockroach roommates? They're quite social - always greeting me in my bedroom at 2 AM and throwing their own little parties in the cabinets. It's like having built-in entertainment!

Now here's the real kicker - y'all already know Texas summers ain't no joke, but this place takes it to a whole new level. Sure, the rent starts at $730 for this 2B2B, but once they tack on all their miscellaneous fees, you're looking at $950 per person. I never knew it was possible for a 900-square-foot space to somehow consume more power than a small factory. Really makes you appreciate candlelight living.

For anyone looking to pay premium prices for a genuine "fixer-upper" experience while actually being a renter, this place is absolutely.

apartments.name: University Place Condominiums
apartments.address: 521 Southwest Pkwy, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Brett Dieterich
recentReviews.text: Great and clean place to stay.  Close to campus and bus route.  Pool and basketball court as well.

recentReviews.author: Josh Fedman
recentReviews.text:
Pros:
* Outside just got a facelift, so it looks pretty nice now.
* Maintenance is usually pretty quick, although we've occasionally had to call and remind them about requests.
* Although the parking lot has a few potholes, parking is plentiful and I've NEVER seen anyone get towed in the 3 years that I've lived here.
* This place is very quiet. There are about 3 parties a year at most.
* Rent is fairly low, although they've been raising it this year.

Cons:
* A few of the building have drainage problems. This means that whenever the sprinklers come on every day, they wash the dirt down into the sidewalk and into the parking.
* Potholes in the parking lot are common and take 6+ months to get fixed.

Our utilities averaged $200-$250, split among 4 people.
Keep in mind that these are condos, not apartments, so things might vary from location to location.

recentReviews.author: Regular Guy
recentReviews.text: The place is very nice for the price. You MAY need to do some detail cleaning. Don't be surprised if you do. Most people are pretty nice and quiet. I found the realtor on craigslist(they are condos so they are owned by investors). There are 4 rooms and each has it's own bathroom. Laundry machines are present inside your floor. Mostly men and woman are separated by floor from what I've  seen. Giving 4 stars due to the lack of our Homeowners association not cleaning things on the outside like mold and rusted through support beams. Overall it is great for the price.

apartments.name: Copper Creek Condos
apartments.address: 301 Southwest Pkwy, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Alondra Alanis
recentReviews.text: I lived here for a whole year and the condition and modernity of the condominium is really great for the price! The Li Family really outdid themselves with offering a great price on a really nice condominium/Alex Li being a great landlord as well. My bathroom, room, and closet were super spacious and my dog loved the private little patio in the back since she was able to go outside and lay in the warm sun. I would have continued living here if I didn't have to go away for a study abroad trip. I would definitely recommend this place to a friend.

recentReviews.author: Sergio Ramirez
recentReviews.text:
UNIT 331, NOT THE TERRIBLE MANAGEMENT ;  Under the management of the Li Family, my 3 years of living at Copper Creek were vastly different than the older reviews here from the old management. I won’t lie to you, they weren’t the most professional or trustworthy people. Thankfully, the Li family saved my roommates and I from the old CC management and we have been satisfied ever since!

They are very attentive and together with their son, all three members of the Li family work hard to make sure we were happily living in our unit. I highly recommend choosing a unit with the Li family.

The unit comes with a backyard, an extra half-bath for guests, big closets, a relaxing bathtub and pool, and it’s next to whataburger. The Li family adds greater value by fixing our issues in the same day, replacing our AC filters monthly, and treating us like friends. I appreciate their help and I hope you will too!

recentReviews.author: Ben Crocker
recentReviews.text: I've lived at Copper Creek for the past two years and have had a great living experience. My unit is managed by the Li family, who are private individual owners. We have had very few problems, but when we have they responded and helped us out very quickly, usually going above and beyond what we expected. It's also in a great location, with a bus stop and restaurants nearby. 10/10 would recommend!

apartments.name: Lakeridge Townhomes
apartments.address: 1198 Jones-Butler Rd, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Lina Farid
recentReviews.text: I’ve lived in Lakeridge with my husband in a 3/3 for almost 5 years now and we have absolutely loved living here. The amenities are great, the pool is our favorite place during the summer, we’ve also used the clubhouse several times hosting our friends for special events like graduation and birthdays. Our condo itself has been lovely, all the devices in the kitchen work so well (microwave, dishwasher, fridge, oven and stove) and the washer and dryer have been great too, never had to fix anything. Same with the AC. Lastly the gated community always made us feel safe and the location, being so close to A&M and on the bus route has been super convenient. Highly recommend living or investing here!

recentReviews.author: Hansong Jiao
recentReviews.text: I have spent two amazing years over here. Everything is fantastic especially the basketball court.

recentReviews.author: Dylan Domagas
recentReviews.text: One of the best places to live in College Station! Location next to multiple bus stops not to mention it is a gated community so I felt safe. Landlord was super sweet and made the renting process very simple. The room is so much bigger compared to other popular apartments like aspire, the rise, and park west to name a few. I definitely liked living here more and for my unit each room has its own individual A/C which was neat, no more arguing over the temperature.

apartments.name: Parcside Townhomes
apartments.address: 2500 Central Park Ln, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: John Vrla
recentReviews.text: Parcside is a good place to live, and management tries its best to make it a good residential experience. We are moving since we don't want a 2 story and found an over 55 apartment that fits are needs better. Parcside is good for young families and would recommend. Hopefully they have plans to update units as they could use it. The kitchen cabinets were just painted over and are all dented up and appliances could use updating too. When you get in the tub shower stall it creaks a lot too. The wall light switches do not work and have to use the pull strings for the fan and light. It would be nice to have a ceiling fan downstairs too. We had the 2-bedroom 2 bath, and it would be good if 1 bath upstairs and 1 bath downstairs. Overall, it's a great started apartment or if looking for something temporary.

recentReviews.author: Jessica Calvin
recentReviews.text:
DO NOT RENT
Our 15-month stay at Parcside Townhomes was deeply disappointing. We endured repeated issues with a broken AC, leaking windows, and a faulty washer which took them 2 weeks to fix. We also had maintenance requests consistently delayed or poorly addressed due to frequent miscommunications with management. The kitchen constantly had roaches that we ended up having to deal with ourselves out of our own pocket because they would not fix it for us. Even though we paid monthly for pest control. Truly a disgusting place to live. Additionally, concerns about a problematic neighbor were ignored, leaving us feeling unheard. The combination of ongoing maintenance problems and management’s unresponsiveness and disrespect made living here stressful and awful. We’re also now dealing with move out fees that are not valid and having to fight those.  I strongly advise potential tenants to consider other options. I would never rent from them again!

recentReviews.author: Lindsey Guillory
recentReviews.text: My husband and I have been living at Parcside for just over a month, and overall we are quite satisfied. What truly brings the rating to 5 stars is Eriele. We worked most closely with her during the paperwork and move-in phases, and she was always positive, friendly, and professional. We also feel that the manager Lauren truly listens to our concerns, and every work order has been addressed swiftly and completely. They are easily the kindest, most responsive front office of any apartment complex I have ever lived at.

apartments.name: Carter Creek Condos
apartments.address: 1451 Associates Ave, College Station, TX 77845, USA

recentReviews.author: Mca
recentReviews.text:
I'm calling on neighbors to be more considerate with parking. Going forward, I'll be prioritizing parking spots closer to my residence, and I may start politely addressing instances where cars are parked outside my door. As a resident who pays a premium rent, I believe it's reasonable to expect a more convenient parking arrangement.

I kindly request that guests park near the pool area.

recentReviews.author: Lisa Gazaway
recentReviews.text: Would definitely recommend this place! My family and I love it! The condos are VERY nice! Nice area and quiet neighborhood! Love the amenities especially the salt water pool! In town and close to everything! The ladies that manage the place have been really helpful and kind to us.

recentReviews.author: Zack Wickens
recentReviews.text: Love the condos! They are so spacious and beautiful! The staff are so friendly and helpful. Amazing people here, would definitely recommend to friends and family if they are looking for a place to stay.

apartments.name: Wolf Creek Condos
apartments.address: 1811 George Bush Dr E, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Wenle Xu
recentReviews.text:
AVOID THEM FOR YOU DEPOSIT!
I had an incredibly frustrating experience when I moved out of this apartment. They imposed a mandatory $338 carpet cleaning fee, which is buried in the lease, and then tacked on an additional $255 cleaning fee for any small stain, no matter how minor. To top it off, they charged me $30 for replacing light bulbs and batteries, which I had already replaced before moving out.

There were also significant issues during my stay. For example, my neighbor’s water pipe burst, flooding my apartment in the middle of the night. The management took 2-3 days to fix it, and they left my place a mess without so much as an apology for the inconvenience.

When I checked the move-out report, I was shocked to see charges for things that never existed, including fees for an imaginary pet I never had and a non-original shower head that I never changed. They even tried to charge me for hangers left behind by the previous tenant, which they deliberately didn’t remove just to add another charge when I moved out.

If you’re considering moving in here, be prepared for unjustified charges and poor service. I definitely would NOT recommend this place unless you’re okay with being nickel-and-dimed for every little thing.

recentReviews.author: Ding Kevin
recentReviews.text: Great experience! Best place that I rented ever. The service requests are resolved quickly. Nice environment also. I would love to continue renting here

recentReviews.author: Jacob Hale
recentReviews.text: I’ve lived here for two years and renewed for a third. Really enjoy living here. Nice sized townhouses that aren’t super fancy but still modern and clean. Assigned parking with plenty of spots for visitors. Quiet area but still close and convenient to A&M campus. Cable and internet included and washer/dryer in unit. Maintenance is quick to respond if there are any issues.

apartments.name: Treehouse Apartments and Condominiums
apartments.address: 200 Marion Pugh Dr, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: M Khan
recentReviews.text:
If you’ve seen 5 or 4-star reviews for The Tree House Apartment, don’t be deceived — it’s likely part of their business strategy. They offer a $100 discount to tenants in exchange for positive feedback, which clearly influences the ratings. But don’t let that fool you, because the reality of living here is far from impressive.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience at The Tree House Apartment. Despite reaching out to the management over 10 times in the past 3 months with requests for essential repairs and maintenance, absolutely nothing has been done. It’s frustrating that after multiple follow-ups, the management has completely ignored these concerns. They are unresponsive, unprofessional, and clearly have no regard for their tenants' comfort or well-being.

Living here has been a hassle, and it's hard to understand how a property can be so poorly managed. The lack of action on simple issues like broken fixtures, leaking pipes, or even general upkeep is unacceptable. It’s clear that the management doesn't care about providing a safe, livable environment.

I would not recommend this apartment complex to anyone. The lack of responsibility and care from the management makes it an overall negative experience.

recentReviews.author: Izzy Ketchens
recentReviews.text: Maintenance is crappy, doesn't fix things in a timely manner an if it's something they don't know about, they won't at all. We had a black mystery sludge coming from our walls an all we got was a "Oh idk just clean it an we'll come back if it continues." Spoiler: it came back but they didn't. Had two gallon milk jugs sitting in the parking lot since June of 2024. The maintenance man lied to the property manager on us saying our apartment was trashed with hair everywhere (I had just cut my hair THAT day IN the bathroom an just hadn't cleaned it up yet, an he said it was trashed cause I moved a recently bought shoe box an had cat toys everywhere). This prompted the property manager to tell us to get rid of the cats (we didn't) and THEN was gonna kick us out, even if we had relocated our cats. Yes we had one more pet than was the lease allowed but they knew that when I moved in with my partner an they said nothing then. There were reaches, and we asked for an exterminator to come out TWICE an they never did. Yes, it's close to campus. Yes, it's cheap. That's why it's cheap, an the property manager will just jack your rent without warning after your initial lease. No, it's not a good place.

recentReviews.author: Maddie Wynn
recentReviews.text: Wonderful affordable apartment close to campus! Managers are awesome and quick to respond, application process was quick and easy, maintenance is also fairly quick. I have a renovated apartment with flooring and it’s very nice clean and comfortable, my dog also enjoys the balcony! Free covered parking is also a huge plus :)

apartments.name: Fox Run Condominiums
apartments.address: 801 Luther W St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: keith miller
recentReviews.text: One star bc your pretty much guaranteed to have your condo flooded by subpar waterlines that are VERY prone to random leaks. Buyers beware. Some units have been re plumbed but you can't replace all of it. (Plumber of 13 years) units themselves are very nice and pool seems to be well maintained.

recentReviews.author: Daniel
recentReviews.text: Your experience will be dependent on the owner of your unit so make sure you schedule a tour before signing

recentReviews.author: Tamara Ospina-Vega
recentReviews.text: Closed from campus, clean, nice pool, great neighbors and a lot of visitors parking lots for your friends!!!

apartments.name: Northpoint Crossing
apartments.address: 1501 Northpoint Ln, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: xtx fk
recentReviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience living here. When we first moved in, the dishwasher was already broken. Despite submitting multiple maintenance requests, it was never repaired during the entire year of my stay.

Elevator maintenance was also a serious issue. One of the elevators stopped working in December 2024 and remained out of service until I moved out in July 2025.

The building is located at a busy intersection, and the noise level is quite high due to very poor sound insulation.

In addition, the rent advertisement was misleading. It claimed to be around $700 per month, but residents are required to pay the full month’s rent even if they stay for only a couple of weeks. As a result, you end up paying more than an extra month’s rent over the course of a year.

There were also repeated charges that seemed unreasonable. For example, I was charged $15 each month for “trash violations,” even though I always followed the building’s trash disposal rules.

Overall, the combination of poor maintenance, excessive noise, and unclear billing made this one of the most disappointing rental experiences I’ve had.

recentReviews.author: Anna Wang
recentReviews.text: I moved out last semester and anytime someone brings up Northpoint i still get the chills. First off management tried to scam me into paying a $3500 security deposit… no one else I knew living there had this happen to them. It took almost two months to resolve this issue and was the worst getting into contact with the workers.They did end up owning up to their mistake and “didn’t know how that happened…” And when they refunded, it was refunded as credit towards paying off rent instead of back to the original payment method. The management team will approach you with attitude and would roll their eyes at me anytime i wanted to address anything wrong. Within first month of living there our apartment flooded for two weeks on and off maintenance were slow and the water that flooded ended up creating damage and upon moving out they tried to charge me for the flooring damage. Our dryer was also broken for a period of time. We were told we would get a latch on our door and never ever got it. When emailing them about our issue the email wrote they would reinstate a credit back to our accounts for the inconvenience also never happened.. Upfront rent would seem reasonable. I think our rent was told to be 850/month but what they don’t disclose is the separate 150 in hidden fees. Only pro to this place is the location but there are plenty of better options on where to live. DO NOT LIVE HERE!
