A lot of people will say not to listen to reviews because it’s only people who had a bad experience but i can attest everyone around me who lived or has lived at Northpoint crossing did not like their time here.

recentReviews.author: Andrea O.
recentReviews.text: I've lived at Northpoint Crossing for about 3 years now, and overall, I have really enjoyed my stay. Its proximity to campus is really nice, and the amenities are also a big plus. Any time we have had an issue, maintenance is quick to come fix it. I definitely recommend living here.

recentReviews.author: JC Zark
recentReviews.text: Nice, quiet place; plenty of parking; interior serves 2 with good space; pool is nothing to write home about.

recentReviews.author: Brook Powell
recentReviews.text: Would really love to inquire about leasing here but no contact information is listed online.

recentReviews.author: james callahan
recentReviews.text: Cozy, quiet, lots of vegetation

recentReviews.author: Nathaniel Johnston
recentReviews.text: The condos here are of decent quality but the surrounding greenery that has absorbed some of the complex and the hidden away feel make this complex seem like it's a bit more run-down than the surrounding area. Prices are fair for what you're getting and the proximity to local attractions and campus are a solid plus.

recentReviews.author: Nigel Flores
recentReviews.text: Love the quiet up kept neighborhood. Very nice condo!! Love my new haven!!

recentReviews.author: Robert Sweat
recentReviews.text: Well kept

apartments.name: The Aria at College Station
apartments.address: 117 Holleman Dr W, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Sarah
recentReviews.text:
This is a long one, but an important one for everyone about to arrive back in town for the school year. There’s no denying this complex is one of the older and more run down complexes for students, and I know construction and renovations are always a hassle while they are going on, and am thankful for them as the complex desperately needed it. I also understand that summer is the best time to do them. However, this has been an absolute nightmare due to the complete breakdown of communication and accountability. What was supposed to be a 2-3 week renovation that was set to start the day after school was out, has now turned into an entire summer and likely entire semester ordeal. Things at the complex look horrific. Trash everywhere. Construction workers blasting music and being incredibly loud early in the mornings. The pool we have all been paying for all year was closed the first week of June, and was supposed to be redone and opened up again in a few weeks. It is now August and the pool has sat completely untouched all summer with no renovation date in sight. Additionally, the gym has also been closed this entire summer (not that anything worked in there before). They have closed half the parking lot off to repave. It’s now been over 2 weeks of parking almost a football field away to get to your apartment, with the parking lot still sitting untouched. I feel horrible for all the people that are moving in right now and can’t park anywhere near their building. I can’t even imagine what it will be like in a few weeks. They only allow you to get packages from 2:30-4:30pm M-F ONLY, so you cannot get packages if you have a job. Trash trucks can’t get to the dumpsters because of the barricades so they haven’t been picked up for weeks and now the parking lots and apartments smell of rotting trash. It is a constant pattern of them destroying something, and then leaving a half started job for weeks for the residents to deal with in the meantime.

The reason this is such a problem is because we have yet to receive a SINGLE email about any of this. If I wasn’t living here and watching it, I wouldn’t even know there was construction at all. No updates, no timelines, no apologies. Not even acknowledging how incredibly horrible this has all been handled. The worst and most outrageous part is the office has been closed indefinitely for over 2 months. There is no working website, no phone number, no working email. Literally no one working here. All the staff has left. It’s just residents. The only communication they do make sure is up to date is their portal to collect rent (which is still full price).

This entire process has been one of the worst living experiences I have ever had. If we were all just kept in the loop and maybe at least just received an email letting us know they are aware of the living conditions at the complex, it would make the situation better. The only reason I even know any details concerning the construction is from contractors stopping to say how bad they feel for us. This has been an incredibly disrespectful process to everyone who is living here this summer, and honestly I have hated every second of it. Especially the amenities like the pool being closed. What was the point of paying for them this entire time if we couldn’t even use them once school let out? For anyone about to move back here for the fall, be ready for trash everywhere, ongoing construction, an empty office, and zero communication. There is no way this will be done by the Fall. They haven’t even started most of what they said they will be doing. Buckle up, this semester is going to be a rough one.

recentReviews.author: Martin Maschio
recentReviews.text: Absolutely the worst place to live at. The new management that came in to this place has been terrible. 0 communication, 0 updates on any renovation projects. Repavement has been going on since the end of the last school year and it is still not done, along with the pool and gym being closed for months with 0 updates. No one ever answers emails or phone calls. Package pickup is only from 2-4 pm M-F so good luck picking anything up if you are  a student or if you have a job. Apartments came with missing towel racks, broken showers and lights. Worst of all though, the vents had been accumulating mold for months. Since move in I've been breathing in mold which is absolutely disgusting. This is nothing like the old Gateway that used to be here that the old reviews talk about. The new management and owners are absolutely terrible. Highly suggest finding other places to live.

recentReviews.author: Harshavardhana Srinivasan
recentReviews.text:
I want to share my huge disappointment with the current management. I was a previous resident here, and ever since the new management took over , it has been a frustrating experience.

As per Texas policy, refund checks should be issued within 30 days. I know that sometimes delays can happen, but in my case it’s already been over 50 days and I still haven’t received mine. Most of my friends got their refund checks enclosed with the notification letter, but in my case I only received the notification letter without the check.

When I tried to get clarification, the responses I got were very vague, and honestly, sounded as arrogant. To make it worse, they hardly ever pick up calls and don’t provide proper updates. I have proof of everything ; the letter, the email conversations, etc. From what I can see, they clearly missed sending my check the first time, and only after I asked multiple times they said that it was mailed again. Even now, I haven’t received it.

I am leaving College Station by October 1, and as of today there is still no check. I’ll have to look for other ways to get this sorted out. Overall, this has been completely unprofessional and shows very poor management.

apartments.name: The Lofts at Wolf Pen Creek
apartments.address: 614 Holleman Dr E, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Magdaline Loop
recentReviews.text:
Coming from a current resident: Please listen to the reviews and do not sign here.

I signed for a year and move out in 9 days and I can’t get out fast enough. Obviously like any other apartment complex, it has its pros and cons. The amenities such as the gym and pools are nice, and the fact that it’s furnished with washers and dryers are nice, but everything else is horrible. The entire complex is ALWAYS dirty, the pavement being stained and foul smelling liquids spilled in the hallways, dead bugs, etc.

There was a week where the fire alarm would go off every 2-3 hours, including throughout the night and the only explanation we got was after day 4 they said they were “looking into the issue”. You literally could not sleep.

I was sitting on my couch one evening and I heard water dripping and I look up to see a hole in my ceiling dripping water. I called emergency maintenance and the guy came out and put A BUCKET and left it there for A WEEK. When I called, they said that the ticket had been incorrectly marked “complete” and it then took them another 6 days to come fix it. It left my cabinets moldy and there’s still a spot where it’s not entirely patched up.

The internet will go out for days at a time. They ended up switching companies about 3 months ago and they are still accessing our units to “try and resolve the ongoing issues”. It does not work in certain parts of the apartment and is unreliable in all others. As someone who just finished their junior year at A&M, this was horrible during finals season.

Another issue is safety. The doors and door codes break all the time and are constantly left open to the public. They are poorly maintained to the point I’ve been locked out of my apartment multiple times due to malfunctioning keypads.

The last thing I’m going to mention is the trash service. I bought a brand new doormat to place outside my door and awoke one morning to it being ruined. They place my trash can directly in front of my door on my door mat go cover a huge, garbage smelling stain and scratches. I’ve reached out to the apartment complex to try to resolve this and but I doubt they will answer as they never do.

The people who work at the front desk are amazing and I am not faulting them at all. Logan has been so helpful, as well as Jacob. It is the management company and managers.

Please, if you are a student or parents of a student looking for a place live, do not sign here. The price is not worth it and you can find much better options elsewhere.

recentReviews.author: Jake Troop
recentReviews.text: Overall, not a bad place to live for the pricing and distance away from campus. It has had its issues, such as the internet problems and the strange trash pickup system. However, compared to other apartments that are either super expensive or super cheap, the Lofts is a solid middle ground complex that is decent and a good spot to live based on location and the services. Been here for three years, so it's a pretty solid choice considering that I have stayed with them for so long.

recentReviews.author: Carli Cook
recentReviews.text: My roommate and I loved living here. Getting to campus is super accessible, as well as the location of the apartment is perfect if you’re a foodie. Since it’s practically on Texas Avenue, it’s super easy to get to restaurants, stores, and parks with walking trails!! The front desk staff is so helpful, and one of the main reasons why my roommate and I decided to re sign for the next year!! Cameron, Megan, Mateo, and Heaven are always so helpful and friendly and the entire staff in general does an awesome job at building those personal relationships with each resident.

apartments.name: Thomas Park Lofts
apartments.address: 1026 Foster Ave, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Alex Newcomer
recentReviews.text:
Not the luxury apartment they market it as. Way too expensive for all of the issues we had.

You would think a "luxury" property management company would want to stand apart from the competition by providing great services for their renters. But that would be too logical!

If you care about timely service responses, privacy (safety if you are a woman) , and getting your deposit back, I would advise you to find a private landlord instead of this company.

We rented a unit at Thomas Park Lofts, which had starting with management under Aggieland property management, which actually did a better job and had great communication. When Terrance Murphy bought the units and Patriarch took over, it all went downhill.

First off, communication from Patriarch only came in the form of long email essays that were clearly written by ChatGPT, if you had a question it would take days to get a response and usually it would come at odd hours like 2am or 4am. They could never pick up the phone. When I went to give the keys back, I had to WAIT 30 MIN for them to communicate where to leave the keys at their office because nobody was working on site.

The 2 times my girlfriend and I had a maintenance request, there was zero communication about the times they would show up and they showed up unannounced (not the plumbers fault). I got a call at work saying plumbers were at my house and I needed to let them in. Of course this was rescheduled. When the plumbers came at a time I could be home, they told me they were told to go anytime cause we would be there...is Patriarch surprised we had to work to pay expensive rent??

Additionally, there were 3 times we did not request maintenance  but Patriarch maintenance or unauthorized pest control entered the apartment without giving notice. We know this because a pest control card was left on our counter and another time a vent was installed on our patio. This is unacceptable, especially due to the fact my girlfriend was sometimes home alone.

Onto the deposit. Our unit was in ok condition when we received it. Nothing a normal person would complain about and they actually redid the floors before we moved it which was fantastic. Aggieland property management did a great job.

When we moved out we had clear communication with Patriarch that 1. We would love to do a walkthrough to identify issues of concern, and 2. Patriarch themselves saying we did not need a professional carpet clean because we did not have pets. We got the apartment cleaned and made sure to even wipe the fans blades. That's how detailed we got upon move out. I would say the apartment was in better shape than we got it, however there was a piece of the patio door that was broken.

This money was important to us and we did everything we could to ensure almost full return of our deposit.

Patriarch must've assumed we would forget about the deposit because there was 0 communication about it after move out. We asked persistently over the next month and a half. They could not seem to communicate the status or what the hold up was. It took well beyond the 30 days allotted for them to send the deposit.

We received less than half of the security deposit back!! The 2 itemized items were "Cleaning; full unit cleaning" and "make ready touch up paint and supplies". What "luxury" property management company has touch up paint as their most expensive line item?? I have never had a landlord charge me for this ever.

The final issues we had are that the hallways and general cleanliness of our building were not up to standard for the rent we were paying. Aggieland property management used to send a person to come clear trash away from the building before it piled up, because the trash cans were so small. But this was too much work for Patriarch.

I was going to give Patriarch a chance to redeem themselves with the deposit, despite all we have been through. STAY AWAY

recentReviews.author: Andrea Johnson
recentReviews.text: Great location! Super close to campus, the staff is always friendly, and the property is very quiet—perfect for studying or relaxing.

recentReviews.author: Laura Johnson
recentReviews.text: Beautiful apartment but it's very expensive. Also be warned that the owners will steal your deposit. They claimed that they needed to repaint the apartment and use a very expensive brand. I have contacted other tenants who also had their deposits taken, even though they made sure the apartment was spotless when they left. Take photos of the apartment before and after living here so you can take them to court if need be.

apartments.name: Warehouse and Factory Apartments at Northgate
apartments.address: 418 College Main St, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Donald Adams Tovar
recentReviews.text: Hi guys just wanted to let you know that they gave me an incredible discount, not just for one month, but for all the months on the contract. The maintenance team is also very fast and kind they fixed a couple of issues in the same hour.

recentReviews.author: Gabby Morgan
recentReviews.text: We’ve only lived here for a few weeks but so far my roommate and I love it! Zoe in the front office was amazing with helping sign our leases and has been a delight since we’ve moved in! They are down to a solo man maintenance team but he is doing amazing! We see him running from apartment to apartment always with something different to fix, but always with a positive attitude and a smile on his face!

recentReviews.author: Carly Peterson
recentReviews.text: The reason I wanted to live here was that it was close to campus, but it was not worth it. The management is all over the place and never has it together. They'll tell you one thing and the opposite. and will be rude while talking to you. There are bugs all over the apartment. My unit has a flea infestation, and they did nothing about it. I have scars all over my body from flea bites, and then I went away for the summer, and the fleas mysteriously were gone. There is a horrible fly problem year-round, and bugs are all in the courtyard. None of the equipment works properly. My microwave, sinks, AC, and lights were all broken, and they never fixed them. It is extremely hot during the first semester and extremely cold during the second semester. They will force you to finish out your lease without any way to get out of it except eviction. I tried to sublease my unit 3 different times, and each time the apartment told me that everything was good, and then suddenly the sublease would fall through. On my final attempt to sublease, they told me everything was confirmed, and I moved out, and then they told me I would still be forced to pay out my lease. I wasted thousands of dollars because they could never finalize a sublease agreement despite telling me everything was okay. This place is NOT worth the money, and they overcharge for everything. The rent and parking are ridiculous considering the apartment is old and they haven't updated or barely fixed any of the issues in my unit.

apartments.address: 4004 Old College Rd, Bryan, TX 77801, USA

apartments.name: University Square
apartments.address: 313 Lincoln Ave, College Station, TX 77840, USA

recentReviews.author: Pardis Taghavi Gilani
recentReviews.text:
I signed the lease almost two years ago because of the wonderful management team they had at the time. Unfortunately, all of those people are now gone, and the new management has been awful.

I moved out of my apartment about two months early, and while I fully understood I’d still be responsible for rent and electricity until the end of the lease, today I received an electricity bill twice of what I expected. When I called to understand what happened, they told me they had set the AC to 69°F and that I would be responsible for the electricity costs based on their preferred temperature. Their staff was smiling behind the phone telling “I assure you ma’am that the temperature of AC doesn’t affect electricity bill price”.

I wanted to share my experience here because many students choose this apartment complex for the location—but it’s important to know it doesn’t worth it. The apartments have also gotten really old, the electricity costs are extremely high.

recentReviews.author: Sierra Schraml
recentReviews.text:
When I moved into my unit it wasn’t actually cleaned from the previous tenants. The stovetop had grease in it and there was human hair in my sink. I also had the bodies of bugs on my windowsill. When I reported it they dismissed me and said it was due to furniture moving. That first night I found the biggest roach I’ve ever seen in my bathroom. I have been battling roaches ever since. Even with weekly reports and biweekly spraying I find them crawling over my apartment at night. It’s genuinely disgusting.

Over the summer, the pool maintained a Kelly green color so no one dared swim. Or sit given the pool is 4 feet deep at max. You’ll also spend a fortune on your electricity bill as there is little to know insulation in the walls. I got to confirm this when my unit flooded and they put holes in my wall for over a month.  The location is great but it’s not worth price of electricity or the roach infestations.

recentReviews.author: Mckenzie Mason
recentReviews.text:
I would recommend University Square for anyone looking for a affordable and good quality apartment to live in. The floor plans are vary spacious, minus the kitchen being on the small side. One thing I greatly enjoyed about the the quality of the building is that the shared walls with neighbors were very soundproof. I could barley hear my neighbors to the side or even the one above me make any sound. Occasionally I would need maintenance done in my apt, the gentleman they have helping them is very professional and knowledgeable. I did have some issues with one of the part time managers on site, however the property manager and I were able to sort out the issue very quickly. I've lived in quite a few apartments to know, every apartment complex will have some issues. This one buy far beats them all out the water for how accommodating and understanding the service is at this location.

I lived at University Square from August 2019 to July 2020. I moved out due to accepting a job requiring me to relocate.

apartments.name: The Cottages of College Station
apartments.address: 2300 Cottage Ln, College Station, TX 77845, USA

recentReviews.author: Abroad Travel
recentReviews.text:
The Cottages - College Station

On the day of my tour it was a little chaotic here. Save your time by not touring the model unit. My pics are of the model unit.

They had students lined up, outside and inside to get new keys or other issues. Some, I heard mentioned their key fob doesn’t work and they can’t get inside their unit. Others, stating they weren’t getting hot water in the shower. Still others, mentioned about bugs problems or that the model unit they saw wasn’t their actual unit layout.

While I was waiting in line to tour the model unit, I noticed there was a dead bird laying outside by pool area that looks like it’s been there a while. After fifteen minutes past my scheduled tour, someone finally showed me the model unit.

Of course, it looked great and perfect. Everything was nice and tidy. No blemishes. I then asked, “Is it possible to tour a unit that’s not a model home?” “Unfortunately, our policy doesn’t allow us to show you what your unit might look like.” I respected that but it was concerning that you’d get into something sight unseen.

I got back in my car and just about to pull away, when I noticed a college student walking by. “Excuse me, would it be possible for me to see your unit? I tried to ask leasing staff and she mentioned she had non available to show, and or they’re not allowed.”

“Yes, of course I can show you,” he replied. Once we got inside his unit, him and his roommates were cleaning the place. After asking them some questions, overall they were satisfied but they didn’t like that their unit had paint on the floors and some other minor issues, including bugs. (To respect their privacy, I didn’t take pics of their apartment)

Yes, this place does get very mixed reviews. Reviews are like a rollercoaster ride here. Location didn’t seem that bad. Some of the amenities seemed good too.

But, the fact that weeks have gone by and I’ve opted out of receiving messages from them. They were persistent to continue sending them. I finally blocked them. I can’t say I’d recommend this place.

recentReviews.author: Quentin HOUPERT
recentReviews.text: I’ve had a great experience living at The Cottages of College Station. The housing itself is very nice and comfortable, and I’ve always felt safe on the property. The amenities, like the pool and the gym, are excellent and make student life much more enjoyable. The maintenance team is also very responsive and quick to help whenever needed. As an international student, I had no problem securing this housing, which made the transition much easier for me. I definitely recommend it!

recentReviews.author: Lauren Serrano
recentReviews.text:
Living at this apartment complex was an overall horrible experience. From the very start, we dealt with countless issues. The unit was filthy when we moved in, with mold everywhere—especially on the vents. Our washer and dryer didn’t work, our stove either barely heated or overheated so badly it burned pans on the lowest setting, and the water boiler constantly gave us problems.

Things seemed slightly better once new management took over, but the problems never truly stopped. Now that I’ve moved out, they are charging me $225 for a bedroom door replacement—the same door their own maintenance team had to screw shut just so it would close properly. I repeatedly confirmed with maintenance that I would not be held responsible for their fix, yet here I am being charged anyway.

On top of this, the front office and management were nearly impossible to reach, making every issue even more frustrating. It felt like one inconvenience after another, and frankly, I felt scammed throughout my time living here.

The only reason I’m giving this place 2 stars is because the rooms and closets are spacious. Unfortunately, that’s the only positive thing I can say. The way this place is run, and the constant attempts to rip off college students, are unacceptable.

recentReviews.author: Blayne Bippert
recentReviews.text:
I would give 0 stars if I could.
I’ve never written a negative Google review before, but my experience living at Redpoint College Station from August 2024 through July 2025 has been extremely disappointing and at times, unsafe. I feel compelled to share my experience so others can make an informed decision.
The apartment was okay when I moved in and my first semester here, not many complaints other than the few visitor parking spots that were almost always full during the school year across the whole entire complex from where I live. Another minor complaint I have is rude and unprofessional emails management sent to me. One of the unprofessional emails I received was about room inspections. I have a dog that I keep in my room and they came to inspect my room when I was gone. My roommate refused to let my dog in the living room and I received an email that I refused room entry and that I had broken the contract of the housing agreement when I didn’t even know that had happened because I was not at the apartment during that time (I attached a picture of the email).
The second half of the semester through Summer the apartment has gone downhill fast from having a report of a suspected gunshot within the complex, to vehicle break-ins throughout the entire complex, to having horrible maintenance issues (I attached a picture of the email we got for the suspected gunshot and the vehicle break-ins). I definitely have not felt safe here compared to all of the other apartment complexes I've lived in College Station.
Unfortunately while I have lived here at Redpoint I have experienced very bad maintenance issues and car break-ins. My now fiancé and my car were broken into and money was stolen. The maintenance issue started as water dripping from our kitchen ceiling near the light and water sprinkler. The maintenance here said it was a leak in our sprinkler system and just patched the ceiling… it turned out to be a much bigger issue. A month later it started to do it again and we reported it again. Our pipe to our water heater was leaking a lot of water upstairs which caused over a 100sq ft of our carpet to be wet (which was not replaced by the way) and our ceiling to be saturated with water causing it to drip. I called emergency maintenance in the early afternoon to come check it out because I was worried and they came a little bit later and called a contracting company and said they would be here closer to the night… They ended up showing up to my apartment around 2:00am. CREEPY! Especially being the only girl staying at the apartment and having to wake up early in the morning for work the next day. That was not considerate at all of maintenance to do that to me after being in contact with them multiple times throughout the whole entire night asking if this could be handled the next day instead of at the time it was handled.
Then after all of that they left an enormous hole in our kitchen ceiling for 2 months and our baseboards ripped out up stairs, then decided they wanted to fix it 2 weeks before I moved out and cut the water off for 4 days (I attached a picture of how the ceiling was left for 2 months). At first they gave me a place to stay and use the water but it was not livable at all (I attached pictures of it). After talking to the office about how it was unlivable because I couldn't get to the microwave to use it they ended up giving me a different place to use. Today has been 7 days since the water has been shut off… Thankfully I left the apartment for a 3 day trip so I didn’t have to stay here with no water and just got back to find out nothing has been completed and we have no water (I have attached a picture of an email, no further communication has happened since then...). If I had known how poorly managed and unsafe this complex would be, I would have never chosen to live here. I strongly encourage anyone considering Redpoint to look elsewhere, the stress and issues I’ve dealt with over the last year are absolutely not worth it.

recentReviews.author: Brooke Smith
recentReviews.text: This place doesn't even deserve a star. Maintenance took 3 weeks to fix one single dishwasher. The past tenants had trashed the place and then they charge you for all of the crap they had broken previously. Everything is broken, utilities are sky high, and the staff argues with you night and day when you try to get things fixed. Also the racoons are nightmares! They get into your trash and leave it all over the porch and (you guessed it), maintenance claims YOU are the problem and charge you extra for it.

recentReviews.author: Katherine Arredondo
recentReviews.text:
I lived at this complex for two years, and while the first year was fine, the second year was a nightmare. When my roommate and I transferred units, the house we moved into was disgusting. There was dog hair caked onto the barstools and light switches, blinds with bite marks, a stair railing cracked in half, and a front door with a huge gap in it that wouldn’t close properly. The back patio was still covered in items from previous residents, and the baseboards, crown molding, and laundry area were layered with dirt and lint. There was even mold growing in the closet when we first moved in.

The house itself had serious structural problems. There was a crack in the ceiling on the first floor and a dip in the floor above it on the second floor. Management’s “solution” was to just paint over the crack instead of actually repairing it. When it rained, water would come through the floor, another issue that was never fixed. Our AC constantly froze, and maintenance’s idea of a fix was to take a torch to it. This eventually caused the unit to break completely, leaving us with window units for two weeks, which sent our electric bill through the roof. It took forever to get any compensation.

When outside contractors finally came to replace the AC, we were told someone from Redpoint staff would be present in our home. That was not the case. We came home to find every single light on, every door open, dents and scuffs on the walls, and our personal bathrooms used — dirt left on our bath mats, the toilet seat left up — even though there was a half bath they could have used.

Maintenance was in and out of our unit constantly but rarely fixed anything. Mold began growing on our belongings, but management insisted it wasn’t mold. On top of that, we never felt safe or like we had any privacy. Management came in for what felt like weekly “inspections,” and they also have a key to your home and will use it without notice. One day we came home to random men inside our house fixing a roof leak we hadn’t even been told about. It was incredibly uncomfortable to feel like strangers could be in our home at any time.

When we moved out, despite paying for professional cleaning, we were still charged over $200 for cleaning and “damage” fees. Overall, this complex is poorly managed, unsafe, and completely disrespectful of residents’ privacy.

And yes, the complex will probably respond to this review with the usual “We’re sorry, please contact management” message. But just know that’s all it is — words. They don’t actually fix these issues.

recentReviews.author: Heather Steedman
recentReviews.text: Actually calling for maintenance was good, they responded quickly at least the day after move-in. However, the place was in really bad shape when I got here, something was wrong with nearly every part of my bathroom and there were a lot of light bulbs burned out in the common area as well as a broken power outlet panel. The air vent also hadn’t been changed in what seems like several years. I don’t think they actually check the rooms between tenants.

recentReviews.author: Jay Flemmings
recentReviews.text: Terrible complex in my opinion, lived there two years and the whole time something wasn’t working or needed to be fixed. On top of that there are way more fees than explained when moving in including move out fees, transfer fees to another unit, etc. One of my roommates got a 75 dollar fee for leaving a trashcan in our old unit. I Wouldn’t recommend living here as it’s literal hell with all the bs you go through and them to not caring or do anything about it.

recentReviews.author: Vinit Sehgal
recentReviews.text: Quiet and serene place. The staff is courteous and they keep doing fun activities time to time to keep the residents feel at home. Beautiful pool and great gym. UT is the kind of place you would like to come home to!

recentReviews.author: Kristi Ratz
recentReviews.text: I was here for 2 years (2022-2024).  It's a small, quiet complex, and you get one dedicated covered parking spot.  Plenty of parking for 2nd car or visitor's car in front of all 4 buildings.  I had a couple maintenance issues, and new owners were quick & responsive, getting the issues fixed promptly.  They keep the pool and laundry areas clean, and they are working hard to get all units upgraded.  Reasonable rates and a larger apartment than you would get at some other complexes for the same price.

recentReviews.author: eshita eshaa
recentReviews.text: Very calm,  quite little apartment complex.  People are good here. The management and Rob are very generous people. Whenever I encountered any issue,  they solved it showing great priority.  The apartment area is neat and clean.

recentReviews.author: Janet Theaker
recentReviews.text:
I lived in this complex for several years. It was my home, I loved the size and price of my apartment. You couldn’t find a more roomy and affordable living space anywhere else in B/CS.  Close to all shopping locations. Literally a stones throw from campus. Covered parking spaces in the back of the complex, plenty of off street parking in the front also. My apartment was a 2 bedroom, one bath unit, I loved it.
So affordable and roomy if you are a student willing to share with a roommate. The complex is also very quiet, great for those long nights of studying.
The owners of the complex also manage it. They are two wonderful and very outgoing people. If you have an issue/repair, don’t hesitate to ask. It will be taken care of usually within 48 hrs, barring the weekend.
I retired a couple of years ago and moved away but I wouldn’t give a second thought to moving back here if the need arose.
